messages.author: fadfb67212d8ec0f
messages.subject: colext: Problems handling missing values?
parts:
Hello unmarked users,

 

A couple of months back I posted about a concern about getting different parameter estimates using the same data when using PRESENCE vs unmarked (re: “colext: differences in unmarked vs. PRESENCE estimates”). Recently I did a bit more exploration and need your help interpreting and deciding next steps. Below, I graphed the yearly parameter estimates for extinction and colonization for a subset of my study period (13 years) using both unmarked (purple) and PRESENCE (orange). The naїve estimate (hand-calculated) is the green line. SE’s are not shown.




This discrepancy led me to ask, “why are the two programs giving me different parameter estimates for the same data?” I suspected it had something to do with the large amount of missing values (NAs) in my dataset. Perhaps the two programs weren't treating missing values in the same way. Further, it appeared from the graphs above that PRESENCE was more closely tracking the naïve estimate than unmarked.  

 

To investigate this question, I created a realistic dataset, seen below. 20 sites, 5 years, 4 surveys/year.




I then fit two occupancy models to the dataset: all constant (~1, ~1, ~1, ~1) and full time dependent (~1, year-1, year-1, year-1). I repeated this 9 times, each time replacing 5 observations from each season with an “NA” entry, so that I fit models with 5, 10, 15, 20, 25, 30, 35, and 40 missing values per season.

 

Below I show the graphs from each of these rounds of model fitting (here, the full-time model): 

PRESENCE = orange, unmarked = purple.


Note: in the first row, when the # missing values = 0, the two programs perform identically.




The two programs’ parameter estimates (on average) diverge as more missing values occurred in the data. Below, I averaged the difference in real parameter estimates (across psi, gamma, eps, p) between the two programs at each missing value level to try and visualize this difference:




In other words, the more missing values, the more the programs performed differently.

 

I realize this is just a cursory investigation of a perceived problem. Can anyone help me clarify what is happening, and help me get on the right track? Ultimately, I’m not that interested in highly parameterized models where I am estimating yearly col/ext. However I feel that whatever is going on here may influence the fit of my models when I use covariates I'm interested in.

 

Help?

messages.author: 4a15de51da4445ae
messages.subject: Re: [unmarked] colext: Problems handling missing values?
parts:
hi Gavin,
 
 This is interesting (also unsettling a bit).  My working hypothesis would be that what you're seeing here is extreme sensitivity to starting values as the frequency of missing values increases.  I'll get in touch with Jim Hines and ask him whether PRESENCE is using a specific rule that might produce good starting values.
 Also I wonder if you could inspect and summarize some of the optimization statistics for these runs, especially at the high missing value end of things?  i.e., does the algorithm converge and produce real standard errors (or NaN/Inf type things).

 

regards
andy

 Also I wonder if you could inspect and summarize some of the optimization statistics for these runs, especially at the high missing value end of things?  i.e., does the algorithm converge and produce real standard errors (or NaN/Inf type things).

 

regards
andy



On Mon, Jun 9, 2014 at 4:31 PM, Gavin M. Jones <gmjo...@gmail.com> wrote:

Hello unmarked users,

 

A couple of months back I posted about a concern about getting different parameter estimates using the same data when using PRESENCE vs unmarked (re: “colext: differences in unmarked vs. PRESENCE estimates”). Recently I did a bit more exploration and need your help interpreting and deciding next steps. Below, I graphed the yearly parameter estimates for extinction and colonization for a subset of my study period (13 years) using both unmarked (purple) and PRESENCE (orange). The naїve estimate (hand-calculated) is the green line. SE’s are not shown.




This discrepancy led me to ask, “why are the two programs giving me different parameter estimates for the same data?” I suspected it had something to do with the large amount of missing values (NAs) in my dataset. Perhaps the two programs weren't treating missing values in the same way. Further, it appeared from the graphs above that PRESENCE was more closely tracking the naïve estimate than unmarked.  

 

To investigate this question, I created a realistic dataset, seen below. 20 sites, 5 years, 4 surveys/year.




I then fit two occupancy models to the dataset: all constant (~1, ~1, ~1, ~1) and full time dependent (~1, year-1, year-1, year-1). I repeated this 9 times, each time replacing 5 observations from each season with an “NA” entry, so that I fit models with 5, 10, 15, 20, 25, 30, 35, and 40 missing values per season.

 

Below I show the graphs from each of these rounds of model fitting (here, the full-time model): 

PRESENCE = orange, unmarked = purple.


Note: in the first row, when the # missing values = 0, the two programs perform identically.




The two programs’ parameter estimates (on average) diverge as more missing values occurred in the data. Below, I averaged the difference in real parameter estimates (across psi, gamma, eps, p) between the two programs at each missing value level to try and visualize this difference:




In other words, the more missing values, the more the programs performed differently.

 

I realize this is just a cursory investigation of a perceived problem. Can anyone help me clarify what is happening, and help me get on the right track? Ultimately, I’m not that interested in highly parameterized models where I am estimating yearly col/ext. However I feel that whatever is going on here may influence the fit of my models when I use covariates I'm interested in.

 

Help?


--

messages.subject: Re: colext: Problems handling missing values?
parts:
Hi all, I have just done a quick comparison between Presence multi-season model and unmarked colext with the same data and found similar issues as Gavin. Unmarked and Presence give identical results when there are no NAs. In one of my datasets there are about 20% of the detection events missing and unmarked does indeed look different than Presence. 

I tried each of the optimization methods available("Nelder-Mead", "BFGS", "CG", "L-BFGS-B", "SANN") and results were nearly identical for all methods except SANN which seems to not converge properly (large parameter SEs). 

So it is not a function of choice of optimization method, rather it must be the way that the optimization handles NA values?  

Thanks Gavin and Andy and everyone who looks into this for us, I'm very curious as to whether a solution can be identified! 

Jay

messages.subject: Re: [unmarked] Re: colext: Problems handling missing values?
parts:
hi Richard,

 I think Gavin did such simulations, (read up in the thread a bit). The results seem to suggest a mis-handling of missing values in the likelihood in my view (Note: PRESENCE also uses default all-0 starts!). 

 A possibility I hadn't thought of before: With so few sites (I think Gavin's example had few sites) its possible that a high frequency of missing values is inducing non-identifiability.

I'm curious if the weird behavior persists with many sites... (e.g., 100 or more).

 Regardless of what's happening I think people need to be cautious when using colext with many missing values until we figure this out. (note: Marc Kery has done tons of simulations with no missing values and the function is definitely working well in that case).


regards
andy
